choices: The aesthetic experience the audience savors, like a flavor
questions.explain: Rasa means taste or flavor: the distilled emotion an audience enjoys through performance.

questions.q: According to the rasa sūtra, rasa arises from the combination of…
choices: Determinants, consequents and transitory states (vibhāva, anubhāva, vyabhicāribhāva)
questions.explain: Causes, visible signs and passing feelings combine, like ingredients making a flavor.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the five stages of action?
questions.explain: Beginning, effort, possibility of attainment, certainty of attainment, attainment of the result.

questions.q: A playwright plants a small, almost unnoticed detail in the first scene from which the whole action later grows. In the Nāṭyaśāstra's terms, this is the…
questions.explain: The bīja, or seed, is the small beginning from which the whole plot develops.

questions.q: How does classical Sanskrit drama typically end, compared with Greek tragedy?
choices: With the hero's goal attained, and a closing benediction
With a chorus announcing the moral
questions.explain: Plays move toward the attainment of the goal. They don't end in tragic catastrophe.

questions.q: Which statement about the Nāṭyaśāstra's authorship is most accurate?
choices: It was written by Aristotle's student
It was written in the 11th century by Abhinavagupta
It is attributed to Bharata Muni, but its date and authorship are uncertain
questions.explain: Tradition credits Bharata; dates around 200 BCE–200 CE are commonly given, and it may have several layers. Abhinavagupta was a later commentator.

questions.q: A film blends romance, comedy, heroism and pathos, with one feeling dominant and the others supporting it. Which idea best describes that design?
choices: A dominant rasa supported by others
questions.explain: A play is expected to have one dominant rasa with others in support.

ideas: An audience doesn't just feel a character's sorrow; it savors a distilled version of it, as a diner tastes a dish.
A plot's whole action should grow from a small seed planted at the beginning.
The hero passes through five stages: beginning, effort, hope of success, certainty of success, and attainment.
